$comment: AFLDB-ISSUE-093 — canonical acceptance/promotion register for fitzRoy core snapshots.
This file records that a specific set of IMMUTABLE raw artefacts, under a specific
importer/contract version, passed INDEPENDENT full-history validation and is accepted
as the rebuild's canonical core source. It is a promotion record, not evidence: the
acquisition manifests under docs/rebuild-manifests/afltables_fitzroy_core/ remain
untouched historical evidence and are never rewritten to reflect an acceptance.
This file is NOT sufficient to bless bytes. Hand-editing it cannot make a snapshot
acceptable, because tools/migration/import_fitzroy_core.py re-derives every
full-history gate from the contract and the artefacts on disk, re-verifies every
artefact SHA-256 against the acquisition manifest, and remains the sole verdict
authority. What this file adds is BINDING: it pins which acquisition is accepted, and
the hashes and measured fingerprints that must still hold for it to stay accepted.
The acquisition manifest's own `full_history` and `completeness` fields are INERT.
full-history-20260827 self-declared full_history=true while the independent validator
rejected it (the acquirer implemented a smaller gate set than the contract declares).
That manifest is preserved byte-for-byte as the record of that mistake.
2026-09-02 (AFLDB-ISSUE-112): this register now carries TWO entries. full-history-20260827
is RETIRED and historical; full-history-20260902 is the single accepted baseline. The
retirement is a provenance decision, not a semantic one - the successor reproduces every
measured drift gate and identity-scan figure exactly. Each entry states its own reasons.
The rebuild resolves its default core source by selecting the single entry whose
acceptance_status is 'accepted'. Zero accepted entries and more than one accepted
entry are BOTH refusals. There is no 'latest label', filename-ordering or date
tiebreak: deterministic selection among multiple baselines is not defined policy,
so the rebuild fails closed and a human must decide.
retired_statuses (AFLDB-ISSUE-101) declares the lifecycle vocabulary for a baseline
that WAS accepted and has since been replaced by a newer accepted baseline. It is a
policy declaration only: adding it changes no acceptance, no measurement and no
acquisition fingerprint, and the accepted baseline below is untouched. The end-of-
season rollover (tools/db/rollover-season.ts) may set an outgoing baseline only to a
status listed here, and 'accepted' may never appear in this list because that would
break exactly_one_accepted.
'retired' is the ONLY correct value for a superseded baseline. Do NOT use 'candidate'
for one: a candidate is an acquisition that has not yet been accepted, and describing
a validated, previously accepted baseline that way would misstate its history. Every
status other than 'accepted' is equally non-selectable to the rebuild — this list
exists so the retirement is a named decision rather than an arbitrary string.
Never read as a verdict by any part of the supported rebuild path. They are the
acquirer's self-assessment, preserved for audit only.
HISTORICAL, NOT INVALID. This baseline was validly accepted on 2026-08-27 and every
record below is preserved unchanged as evidence: its acquisition manifest
docs/rebuild-manifests/afltables_fitzroy_core/full-history-20260827.json is still
byte-for-byte the original, its hash bindings still describe the bytes it was
granted over, and its measured fingerprint is still the fingerprint this source
must reproduce.
It is retired because its ACCEPTED RAW BYTES ARE UNAVAILABLE. The working copy at
snapshot_dir was lost, and AFLDB-ISSUE-112 Pass 19 proved on 2026-09-02 that a
reacquisition from the pinned adapter cannot reproduce them: 130 of 131 artefacts
re-acquire byte-identically, but player_details.csv does not
(accepted 215d66f72a8aa032a615ffd4b43429e18c6c42d8cdbfae67f8833d87bef51461,
reacquired 62171adf0dba3914afe8e6dbd7a0aa4720a8cd8dec86e10f91b8ab899c1e4a91,
16731 rows and identical columns in both). Two independent acquisitions on
2026-09-02 agree with each other, so this is upstream AFL Tables player-detail
content drift since the 2026-08-27T01:54:19Z extraction, not local nondeterminism.
The changed field cannot be named because the accepted bytes no longer exist to
diff against.
No byte, hash or measurement in this entry was edited to accommodate the
retirement, and the successor was NOT accepted by copying this record: it earned
its own independent --require-full-history verdict over its own bytes. The
successor reproduces every measured drift gate and every identity-scan figure
here EXACTLY, which is why the retirement is a relabelling of provenance and not
a change of canonical semantics.
manifest_sha256 covers the acquisition manifest byte-for-byte, so the artefact
hash list inside it cannot be edited to cover for a tampered artefact without
breaking this binding.

raw_artefacts.digest_rule: sha256 over sorted lines '<filename> <sha256> <row_count>\n' from the acquisition manifest's files[]

$comment: Accepted under AFLDB-ISSUE-112 runbook §28.4 route 2, an explicit operator
decision to MOVE the acceptance baseline rather than restore unreproducible bytes.
This is a new acceptance under the AFLDB-ISSUE-093 §4 immutability rule (a
reacquisition whose bytes differ is a NEW snapshot with its own label, its own
manifest and its own fingerprint), never an in-place replacement of
full-history-20260827's record.
Provenance of the bytes: acquired 2026-09-02T01:00:04Z by the pinned adapter
tools/rebuild/fitzroy/acquire_core.R, fitzRoy 1.8.0 (installed == pinned),
--from 1897 --to 2025, --datasets player_stats,player_details,results, during
AFLDB-ISSUE-112 Pass 19. That pass acquired into an isolated staging root so no
adapter could write near a tracked manifest; the artefacts were preserved off-tree
and promoted here unmodified in Pass 20. They were NOT reacquired for this
acceptance, so the manifest's extraction timestamp is the true extraction time.
Relationship to the retired baseline: 130 of the 131 artefacts are byte-identical
to full-history-20260827. The single difference is player_details.csv
(215d66f7... -> 62171adf...), upstream AFL Tables content drift, same 16731 rows
and identical columns. That one artefact is why the artefact-set digest and the
manifest hash differ, and therefore why this is a new baseline at all.
Why the move is safe: every measured drift gate and every identity-scan figure
below is IDENTICAL to the retired baseline's, re-derived independently from these
artefacts by the sole verdict authority. The acceptance changes provenance, not
canonical semantics.
manifest_sha256 covers the acquisition manifest byte-for-byte, so the artefact
hash list inside it cannot be edited to cover for a tampered artefact without
breaking this binding.
The manifest is the adapter's own Pass 19 output with exactly two byte ranges
changed for the new label: `snapshot_label` and `working_directory`, then newline-
normalised from CRLF to LF. Nothing else differs - not one filename, hash, row
count, column list or observation - and the importer re-hashes all 131 artefacts
against it regardless.
The LF normalisation is MANDATORY, not cosmetic: .gitattributes pins
docs/rebuild-manifests/** to eol=lf precisely because manifest_sha256 above binds
the manifest FILE bytes (AFLDB-ISSUE-108). A CRLF manifest would be rewritten on
checkout and would break this binding on one platform only.
Its self-declared `full_history: false` / `completeness: unvalidated` are INERT,
like every acquisition verdict field. This adapter build correctly declines to
self-assess; the verdict below came from the independent validator.

The raw artefacts, their hashes, the manifest binding and every identity_scan figure
are UNCHANGED. The importer gained the profile_url_continuity transformation
(tools/rebuild/fitzroy/fitzroy-contract.json, tools/migration/import_fitzroy_core.py)
and measured.players therefore moved 13275 -> 13271: the four 2025 profiles AFL

seeding four 2025-only duplicates. distinct_urls stays 13275 because every profile
path is still registered as an external identity of its (now single) player.
Recorded here as a dated amendment to the accepted entry rather than a new
acceptance: the acceptance binds bytes and measurements, both re-derived by the
validator on every run, and the OLD players figure was the one that described a
split identity. Ratification of this amendment (or a decision to re-accept under a

Every value is identical to retired baseline full-history-20260827's EXCEPT

AFLDB-ISSUE-136 (2026-09-04): those five paths are FOUR renumbered profiles of

Identical to retired baseline full-history-20260827's scan.
